variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: The policy gradient theorem explains how to improve a policy: a model that assigns probabilities to actions. It says that an action should become more likely when it produces a better-than-expected outcome, and less likely when it produces a worse one.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Read the theorem as three questions”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Where should the policy move?
pairs.detail: ∇θ log πθ(a | s) points toward parameters that make the sampled action more likely.
pairs.explanation: ∇θ log πθ(a | s) points toward parameters that make the sampled action more likely. For a softmax policy, other actions move in the opposite direction.

pairs.label: How strongly should it move?
pairs.detail: Qπ(s, a), a sampled return G_t, or an advantage A_t weights that direction.
pairs.explanation: Qπ(s, a), a sampled return G_t, or an advantage A_t weights that direction. Positive values reinforce the action; negative values suppress it.

pairs.label: Which experiences count?
pairs.detail: The expectation averages states and actions visited by the current policy.
pairs.explanation: The expectation averages states and actions visited by the current policy. Changing the data-collecting policy changes the distribution behind the gradient.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is that every policy update is a policy-score direction multiplied by an action-quality signal.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Where should the policy move?: ∇θ log πθ(a | s) points toward parameters that make the sampled action more likely. Which experiences count?: The expectation averages states and actions visited by the current policy.

variants.title: Give each part its job

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Derive the estimator without differentiating the environment”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Write the objective
pairs.detail: Express expected return as J(θ) = Eτ~pθ(τ)[R(τ)], where trajectory probability includes the initial state, policy actions, and environment transitions.
pairs.explanation: Express expected return as J(θ) = Eτ~pθ(τ)[R(τ)], where trajectory probability includes the initial state, policy actions, and environment transitions.

pairs.label: Apply the log derivative
pairs.detail: Use ∇pθ(τ) = pθ(τ)∇log pθ(τ) to turn the gradient of an expectation into an expectation of a gradient.
pairs.explanation: Use ∇pθ(τ) = pθ(τ)∇log pθ(τ) to turn the gradient of an expectation into an expectation of a gradient.

pairs.label: Drop environment terms
pairs.detail: Initial-state and transition probabilities do not depend on θ, so only Σ_t log πθ(a_t | s_t) remains inside the gradient.
pairs.explanation: Initial-state and transition probabilities do not depend on θ, so only Σ_t log πθ(a_t | s_t) remains inside the gradient.

pairs.label: Assign future credit
pairs.detail: Rewards before action a_t cannot be caused by that action.
pairs.explanation: Rewards before action a_t cannot be caused by that action. Weight its score only by return from time t onward, producing G_t.

pairs.label: Freeze a behavior version
pairs.detail: Roll out one identifiable policy version and store states, actions, rewards, termination flags, values, and old action log probabilities.
pairs.explanation: Roll out one identifiable policy version and store states, actions, rewards, termination flags, values, and old action log probabilities.

pairs.label: Construct targets
pairs.detail: Compute returns and advantages with correct terminal versus time-limit handling.
pairs.explanation: Compute returns and advantages with correct terminal versus time-limit handling. Normalize advantages over an intentional batch boundary.

pairs.label: Optimize bounded losses
pairs.detail: Combine the actor objective, critic loss, and entropy bonus.
pairs.explanation: Combine the actor objective, critic loss, and entropy bonus. Clip gradient norm and stop early when policy divergence exceeds the release threshold.

pairs.label: Evaluate before recollecting
pairs.detail: Measure reward distributions, constraints, action entropy, critic error, and behavior slices before the new policy becomes the data collector.

variants.prompt: What usually happens as GAE lambda moves from 0 toward 1?
options: The estimator relies on longer TD traces, usually reducing bootstrap bias while increasing trajectory variance
The policy becomes deterministic immediately
The value baseline becomes action-dependent
PPO no longer needs old log probabilities

The term is always equal to the reward
Softmax stops being differentiable above 0.90
The other action has no logit
